Filter the experiment used for a differential fit

step_filter_sig_vars.Rd

In a connected blueprint, attach this step to a differential analysis. Multiple filters can consume one fit with different cutoffs. A successful filter can return an experiment with zero rows.

Usage

step_filter_sig_vars(
  p_adj_cutoff = 0.05,
  p_val_cutoff = NULL,
  fc_cutoff = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

p_adj_cutoff

The threshold for p-adjusted values. Default is 0.05.

p_val_cutoff

The threshold for p-values. We don't recommend using this. Default is NULL. If you insist to use it, please set p_adj_cutoff to NULL.

fc_cutoff

The threshold for fold changes. Only positive value is needed. For example, 2 means fold change > 2 or < 1/2. Explicit NULL disables fold-change filtering for every scale. When omitted, the default is 2 for glycoproteomics comparisons with available fold changes and NULL otherwise. For "logx" results, a non-NULL cutoff warns and is ignored because original-abundance fold changes are unavailable; filtering uses only the selected significance cutoff. Raw-scale gly_limma() results and other gly_linear_model() results reject non-NULL cutoffs.

...

Method-specific arguments for glystats::filter_sig_vars(), such as on = "post_hoc_test" and comparison for ANOVA.

Value

A connected step with a filtered experiment as its main output.

Examples

blueprint(step_dea_anova() %=>% step_filter_sig_vars())
#> Blueprint (root accepts exp)
#> └─ node_1  step_dea_anova() (omnibus)
#>   └─ node_2  step_filter_sig_vars() (filtered_exp)
